My escalation_triggers 2 routes 'the computation to T9', consistent with the 'duty' classification and with keeping ALL duty computation in one specialist. That is internally defensible -- but the question's point stands that, unlike the US-side 6110 duty (which genuinely sits in T9's US-landed lane), this India-side duty sits UPSTREAM of the ex-factory gate and arguably belongs in the fibre-cost read that yarn surfaces and T4 assembles, not the US-landed line T9 owns. The fix does not reconcile this: it asserts 'defer to T9' without addressing that the layer is an ex-factory-upstream input, so I cannot claim the owner is unambiguously correct. Honest position: yarn surfaces the layer and holds it [UNKNOWN] (correct); the DOWNSTREAM owner of the computation is under-specified between T9 (duty lane) and T4 (ex-factory-input lane) and should be resolved explicitly rather than defaulted to T9 by the word 'duty'.

So the instruction mis-fires for the local-house route: there the [UNKNOWN] is simply the local house's delivered rupee price (which happens to embed the duty), not a separately-deferred duty layer, and treating it as an additive layer risks double-counting against that price. The distinction the fix never draws is: the [UNKNOWN]-and-defer-as-a-distinct-duty-layer attaches to the SELF-IMPORT route (brand imports tops, brand/importer bears an itemisable India duty); on the local-house route the duty is embedded and the only [UNKNOWN] is the house's all-in price.
